Ghetto of Verona

Ghetto · Verona, Italy

Indirect sources date the first traces of Jewish presence in Verona to before the 10th Century. In the years following, the city became an important centre for Jewish studies, hosting a number of prominent figures. The ghetto area, situated between what are today Via Pellicciai and Via Mazzini, soon had to be expanded due to successive waves of migration that brought Sephardic Jews from Venice and Marranos, fleeing from the Inquisition, from all over Europe. All that is visible today of the ancient ghetto are a few remains that escaped the urban redevelopment works carried out in the area in the 1920s.
